question: In a COPD patient presenting with an acute exacerbation, high-flow oxygen should be administered at 10–15 L/min via a non-rebreather mask to achieve SpO₂ > 98%.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. In COPD, the recommended SpO₂ target during an exacerbation is 88–92%. High-flow oxygen targeting > 98% can suppress the hypoxic ventilatory drive in CO₂ retainers and precipitate hypercapnic respiratory failure.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. High-flow uncontrolled oxygen in COPD risks hypercapnic respiratory failure by suppressing hypoxic ventilatory drive. The target SpO₂ in COPD exacerbation is 88–92%, delivered via controlled low-flow O₂ (Venturi mask at 24–28%).
